newsitem.title: GERMANY: Hamburg 1996 port turnover down from 1995 record.
newsitem.headline: Hamburg 1996 port turnover down from 1995 record.

text.p: Turnover at the port of Hamburg fell to 71.1 million tonnes in 1996, down 1.4 percent from the 1995 record , a statement from the port promotion office said.
Sharply lower grain exports as well as lower coal and ore imports contributed to the slowdown, which was partly offset by strong container traffic and general cargo growth.
Container traffic accounted for 44 percent of the total and included more soft commodities previously shipped in bags.
Some 74 percent of the sugar, 55 percent of the cocoa and 96 percent of all coffee handled by Hamburg was containerised.
Liquid cargo turnover rose 7.6 percent to 14.1 million tonnes.
Oil products and crude oil imports rose sharply amid higher heating oil demand in the severe 1995/96 winter.
Germany imports one third of its total oil requirements.
The overall suction goods category was off by 13.3 percent at 5.8 million tonnes as grain exports plummeted by 40 percent to 1.62 million tonnes.
Imports of oilseeds and feeds were roughly steady in 1996 but exports were significantly higher than the year before.

Grab goods turnover fell by 13.2 percent to 2.18 million tonnes because iron ore imports dropped amid a steel industry slowdown and because coal and building materials demand eased on problems in the eastern German construction sector.
In addition, a steel mill in Hamburg switched from ore to scrap intake.
The port said it expected to receive more coal, ore and building materials in 1997, when handling levels of grains, feeds and oils should at least stabilise.

Oil imports would continue strong but could stagnate in the long run because planned new refinery capacity in eastern Germany's Leuna, fed via pipeline from Russia, would lessen the relative importance of Hamburg imports.
